problem: VLN training data is limited in diversity and scale because datasets rely on manually curated simulator scenes. Zero-shot EQA as video QA must process large numbers of frames, which is costly, can miss fine-grained details, and causes VLM hallucinations.
motivation: Web room-tour videos offer diverse, real-world indoor scenes and human navigation behavior at scale, but they carry no explicit navigation annotations. For EQA, the visual input needs to shrink to only the frames relevant to the question, and checking answers with reversed question logic may reduce hallucination.
key_idea: Build a large VLN dataset (Room Tour3D) by reconstructing 3D scenes from web room-tour videos and generating trajectories and instructions, and for EQA filter video frames using relevance selection plus reverse question logic (RRL).
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that real-world web-video data improves several VLN benchmarks, and that relevance-based frame filtering with reverse logic cuts visual processing by up to 80% while staying comparable to the baseline on OpenEQA.
method: Room Tour3D dataset: web room-tour videos are converted into about 100K description-enriched trajectories with 200K navigation instructions, plus 17K action-enriched trajectories, across 1,847 environments.
3D reconstruction and trajectory extraction: scenes are reconstructed from the videos to obtain human walking trajectories, room type annotations, object locations, and scene geometry.
Instruction generation: open-ended, open-world navigable instructions are generated for the extracted trajectories.
RRL filtering pipeline: relevance-based frame selection picks the frames most relevant to the question for zero-shot video QA in EQA.
Reverse question logic: a reversed form of the question is used to make VLM answers more robust against hallucination.

setting.backbone: not specified in the abstract (VLN models trained with Room Tour3D; a VLM for the EQA pipeline)
setting.training_data: Room Tour3D (about 100K description-enriched trajectories, 200K instructions, 17K action-enriched trajectories, 1,847 room tour environments) added for VLN; the EQA part is zero-shot
setting.simulator: not specified in the abstract (web-video-derived 3D reconstructions)

results: The abstract reports significant gains on CVDN, SOON, R2R, and REVERIE from adding Room Tour3D, with no numbers given. On OpenEQA, RRL is comparable to the baseline while reducing visual data processing by up to 80%.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so quantitative results and implementation details could not be verified.
The trajectories come from 3D reconstruction of web videos, which may be noisy, and the abstract gives no quality analysis.
compares_to: Prior VLN datasets on CVDN, SOON, R2R, REVERIE
